name: Cape Malay chicken curry
summary: A mild, fragrant chicken and potato curry warmed with cinnamon and cardamom and finished with a touch of sweetness, the way Cape kitchens make it.
about: Cape Malay cooking grew from the food of people brought to the Cape from Indonesia, India and elsewhere from the 1600s. Its curries are gentler and more aromatic than Durban's, with whole sweet spices and a hint of sugar. Chicken and potato curry is the everyday family version, served with rice or roti and a tomato-onion sambal.

ingredients.name: Mild curry masala
ingredients.note: a Cape Malay or mild masala blend

steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat. Add the onions, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves and fry, stirring now and then, until the onions are soft and golden, 8–10 minutes.

Add the curry leaves and the garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in the masala, cumin, coriander and turmeric with a splash of water and cook for 1 minute so the spices lose their raw smell without catching.
Add the chicken and turn it in the spices over medium-high heat for about 5 minutes, until every piece is coated and lightly sealed.
Tip in the tomatoes, water, sugar and salt, stir well and bring to the boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes.

Add the potatoes, pushing them down into the gravy. Cover again and simmer for 25–30 minutes, stirring gently once or twice, until a knife slides easily into the potatoes and the chicken comes away from the bone.

Take the lid off for the last 5 minutes if the gravy is thin, letting it reduce until it coats the back of a spoon. Taste for salt, remove the cinnamon stick, scatter with coriander and serve with basmati rice or roti and a tomato-onion sambal.
prepNote: Tastes even better the next day; cool, refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat gently with a splash of water.
